correctness.rationale: The n-parameter recurrence is positive and self-consistent; coordinate growth is uniformly controlled by the choice theta(D+1)^(n-1)<=1/4; the anchored A_p estimate is a convergent product-geometric series for every p>1; a two-cell rectangle gives the matching characteristic lower bound; the bounded-mass hyperbolic region has cardinality at least c theta^{-1} log^{n-1}(1/theta); and the source-cell test converts those disjoint cells into the claimed L^p lower norm. Coordinatewise averaging and reflection preserve the required A_p control on arbitrary rectangles and on R^n.

originality.rationale: Lerner arXiv:2609.14008v1 proves the logarithmic obstruction only for n=2,p=2. Ombrosi--Rey arXiv:2609.17246v1 treats all p and dimensions on the upper-bound side and still cites only Lerner's planar p=2 logarithmic lower bound. Searches for equivalent all-p/higher-dimensional rectangular-A_p logarithmic lower bounds and current SCOPE overlap found no prior coverage. Residual risk remains from unindexed contemporaneous work because the source papers are very recent.

value.rationale: The result makes endpoint-power failure universal for every n>=2 and 1<p<infinity and identifies a dimension-amplified logarithmic obstruction (log A)^((n-1)/p) arising from an n-parameter divisor count. It supplies substantially more structure than the single known planar p=2 example while remaining compatible with the latest improved upper power bounds.
